# Project Requirements: aTrainingTracker

This document tracks all functional and non-functional requirements of the project. Every code change must be traceable to a requirement defined here.

## 2. Sensor Data Processing & Filtering

| ID | Description | Rationale | Implementation File(s) | Verification ID | Status |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **REQ-FIL-001** | Flexible filtering (Moving Avg, Exponential Smoothing). | Allow for smooth visualization of noisy sensor data. | `FilterManager.java` | `TST-UNT-004` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-002** | Configurable smoothing factors (α) for Power. | Balance responsiveness vs. stability. | `ExponentialSmoothingFilter.java` | `TST-UNT-005` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-003** | Calculate derived metrics (VAM, slope, pace). | Provide advanced metrics for climbing and analysis. | `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice.java` | `TST-UNT-002` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-004** | **Atomic Altitude Correction.** | The system SHALL apply altitude corrections from known locations atomically across all data structures. This MUST include shifting previous sample points, updating summary extrema (Min/Max), and recalculating total ascent/descent for the active workout to ensure 100% data consistency. | `TrackerService.java`, `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java` | `TST-FIL-003` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-005** | Implement "Proxy Sensors" and "Accumulator Sensors". | Extensible architecture for complex multi-sensor data. | `ProxySensor.java` | `TST-STR-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-006** | Geographical rolling averages for start altitude. | Filter out momentary GPS or barometric jitter. | `WorkoutSamplesDatabaseManager.java`| `TST-STR-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-FIL-012** | **Stabilized VAM (Vertical Speed) Metric, Location Accuracy Gating & Indoor Drift Suppression Architecture.** | The system SHALL calculate the vertical ascent/descent rate (VAM / Vertical Speed in m/h) in `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice` using linear regression slope smoothing over a sliding window, suppress indoor GPS wander and stationary drift, enforce location accuracy gating, maintain a noise deadband, and reject outlier anomalies (ATT-1621, ATT-1738):<br>1. *Sliding Window Linear Regression Derivative ($N = 15$ seconds)*:<br>• The system SHALL maintain an equidistant 1-second circular buffer of up to $N = 15$ recent altitude samples.<br>• For a full buffer of $N = 15$ samples, the ascent rate slope $\hat{\beta}$ (in m/s) SHALL be evaluated using least-squares linear regression: $\hat{\beta} = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} w_k \cdot a_k$ where $w_k = \frac{k - \frac{N-1}{2}}{\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} (j - \frac{N-1}{2})^2}$, minimizing total squared error across all samples in the window.<br>• For an initial buffer with $M$ samples ($2 \le M < 15$), the system SHALL evaluate the least-squares slope dynamically over the available $M$ points, enabling immediate responsiveness during warm-up without artificial startup delay.<br>• The unconstrained vertical speed in m/h SHALL be computed as $\text{raw\_vam} = \hat{\beta} \times 3600$.<br>2. *Location Accuracy Gating ($> 20.0\text{ m}$)*:<br>• The system SHALL query horizontal accuracy (`SensorType.ACCURACY`) via `cAccuracyFilter = new FilterData(null, SensorType.ACCURACY, FilterType.INSTANTANEOUS, 1)`.<br>• If GPS accuracy is degraded ($> 20.0\text{ m}$), the system SHALL suppress the calculated vertical speed to `0 m/h` to reject multipath altitude jitter in indoor, basement, or canyon environments.<br>3. *Stationary Gating & Low-Speed Drift Damping*:<br>• The system SHALL query horizontal speed `speed_mps` from `speedFilteredSensorData` and the dynamic minimum speed threshold `minSpeed = SettingsDataStoreJavaHelper.getSlopeMinSpeed(mContext)` (default `0.5` m/s).<br>• If the athlete is stationary (`speed_mps < minSpeed` or `speed_mps < 0.5` m/s):<br>  - If the calculated vertical ascent rate is within typical stationary sensor noise ($|\text{raw\_vam}| < 150\text{ m/h}$, corresponding to $|\Delta h| < 0.2\text{ m}$ over 5s), the system SHALL clamp vertical speed to `0 m/h`.<br>  - If genuine vertical displacement occurs while stationary in the horizontal plane ($|\text{raw\_vam}| \ge 150\text{ m/h}$, such as an elevator, ski lift, or vertical climbing wall), the system SHALL broadcast the measured vertical speed.<br>• If the athlete is moving at low drift/walking speeds ($0.5\text{ m/s} \le \text{speed\_mps} < 1.2\text{ m/s}$):<br>  - The system SHALL enforce an elevated drift deadband ($|\text{raw\_vam}| < 150\text{ m/h}$ clamped to `0 m/h`), preventing phantom GPS wander speeds from triggering false climbing rates.<br>4. *Flat Terrain Athletic Noise Deadband*:<br>• When the athlete is moving horizontally at athletic speed ($\text{speed\_mps} \ge 1.2\text{ m/s}$) with valid GPS accuracy ($\le 20.0\text{ m}$), if $|\text{raw\_vam}| < 35\text{ m/h}$, the system SHALL clamp vertical speed to `0 m/h` to eliminate barometric ripple on flat terrain.<br>5. *Outlier & Physical Boundary Clamping*:<br>• The calculated vertical speed SHALL be clamped to the range $[-3000, 3000]\text{ m/h}$ to prevent single-tick GPS multipath altitude jumps from corrupting downstream recording.<br>6. *Preservation of Invariants*:<br>• `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL broadcast integer values in m/h at 1-second intervals.<br>• Accumulator sensors `SensorType.ASCENT` and `SensorType.DESCENT` using `cAltitudeSuperFilter` SHALL remain completely unaffected.<br>• `SLOPE` calculation using `getSlopeMinSpeed(mContext)` SHALL remain completely unaffected.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-FIL-003` (*Calculate derived metrics: VAM, slope, pace*), implemented in `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Sprint 2026-40.5 (ATT-1621), refined in Sprint 2026-40.6 (ATT-1738).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Stationary gating in ATT-1621 assumed horizontal speed drops below $0.5\text{ m/s}$ when stationary. However, in indoor/basement testing, GPS multipath wander was found to generate phantom horizontal speed ($0.6\text{–}1.5\text{ m/s}$) and large altitude jumps ($\pm 5\text{–}15\text{ m}$), bypassing the stationary check and amplifying noise into erratic $\pm 800\dots 2400\text{ m/h}$ swings.<br>4. *Refinement Reason*: Introducing location accuracy gating ($> 20.0\text{ m}$) and low-speed drift damping ($< 1.2\text{ m/s}$) to suppress indoor GNSS wander while preserving genuine outdoor athletic climbs and elevator/lift vertical movements.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: 1-second emission periodicity, integer m/h units, accumulator integration, and slope calculation invariants are 100% preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete stationary indoors or in a basement with degraded GPS accuracy ($> 20.0\text{ m}$),<br>• *When* GPS altitude fluctuates,<br>• *Then* `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL broadcast `0 m/h` without jumping to phantom positive or negative values.<br>• *Given* an athlete indoors with phantom GPS wander speed ($0.6\text{–}1.1\text{ m/s}$) but minor vertical jitter ($|\text{raw\_vam}| < 150\text{ m/h}$),<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL broadcast `0 m/h`.<br>• *Given* an athlete climbing steadily at 800 m/h ($0.222\text{ m/s}$ vertical speed) with horizontal speed $> 1.2\text{ m/s}$ and accuracy $\le 20.0\text{ m}$,<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* calculated VAM SHALL smoothly converge to $800 \pm 15\text{ m/h}$ and maintain stability without erratic second-by-second swings exceeding $\pm 20\text{ m/h}$.<br>• *Given* an athlete in an elevator or ski lift moving vertically at $\ge 150\text{ m/h}$ while horizontal speed is $< 0.5\text{ m/s}$ and accuracy $\le 20.0\text{ m}$ (or indoor barometric fix),<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* the vertical rate SHALL NOT be suppressed to 0, but accurately reflect the vertical movement.<br>• *Given* an athlete riding on a flat road where minor road vibration or barometric ripple produces $|\text{raw\_vam}| < 35\text{ m/h}$,<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* `mVerticalSpeedSensor` SHALL output `0 m/h`.<br>• *Given* a sudden isolated GPS altitude step anomaly (e.g. +30m jump in 1 second),<br>• *When* VAM updates,<br>• *Then* the calculated VAM SHALL be safely clamped to $\le 3000\text{ m/h}$.<br><br>**Invariants**: 1-second emission periodicity, integer m/h units, accumulator integration, and slope calculation invariants MUST NOT be broken. | Stabilize VAM metric using 15-second least-squares linear regression slope, location accuracy gating, low-speed drift damping, flat terrain noise deadband, and outlier clamping in VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice. | `VerticalSpeedAndSlopeDevice.java` | `TST-FIL-004` | Verified |

## 3. Tracking Logic & Session Management

| ID | Description | Rationale | Implementation File(s) | Verification ID | Status |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **REQ-TRK-001** | Support Start, Stop, Pause with Service persistence. | Ensure data integrity in the background. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-REG-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-002** | **Workout Lap Recording Lifecycle, Manual Splitting & Pause/Resume Neutrality.** | The system SHALL manage the lifecycle of workout laps deterministically during recording, tracking termination, and database retrieval, preventing the creation and presentation of zero-duration phantom laps:<br>1. *Pause and Resume Neutrality*: Transitioning active tracking into a paused state (`pauseTracking()`) or resuming tracking from paused (`resumeFromPaused()`) SHALL NOT broadcast `REQUEST_NEW_LAP` and SHALL NOT create, increment, or close workout laps. Active lap duration and distance accumulation SHALL pause and resume transparently with the session.<br>2. *Manual Lap Splitting Integrity*: Explicit lap requests initiated by the user (via `TrackingViewsRepository.requestNewLap()` in the tracking UI or `BUTTON_LAP` from a connected smartwatch) SHALL finalize the active lap, persist its split metrics to `Laps.db` (`saveLap(...)`), broadcast `BANALService.LAP_SUMMARY`, and initialize the subsequent sequential lap index ($N+1$).<br>3. *Workout Finalization & Termination Guards*: Upon tracking completion (`TrackerService.endWorkout()`), `createNewLap()` SHALL finalize and persist the active in-progress lap if and only if `lapTime_s > 0` or `lapDistance > 0.0`. If the active lap has zero duration and zero distance, the system SHALL discard it and MUST NOT persist it to `Laps.db`.<br>4. *Defensive Database & Receiver Validation*: `TrackerService.mLapSummaryReceiver` and `LapsDatabaseManager.saveLap(...)` SHALL reject any lap record where `timeTotal <= 0 && distanceTotal <= 0.0`, ensuring invalid or empty splits are never written to SQLite.<br>5. *Historical & Vectorized Query Sanitization*: In `LapsDatabaseManager.getLaps(workoutId)` and `getLapsForWorkouts(workoutIds)`, queries SHALL filter out legacy zero-duration records (`TIME_TOTAL_s > 0 OR DISTANCE_TOTAL_m > 0`), ensuring corrupted historical splits do not render in workout summaries (`WorkoutLaps.kt`) or export files (`TCXFileWriter.java`, `GPXFileWriter.java`).<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active live tracking session with no manual lap presses,<br>• *When* the user pauses tracking, resumes tracking, pauses again, and ends the workout,<br>• *Then* `Laps.db` SHALL contain exactly 1 lap record whose duration and distance match the total active workout metrics, with zero 00:00:00 phantom laps.<br>• *Given* an active live tracking session where the user explicitly taps "New Lap" once at minute 10 and ends the workout at minute 25,<br>• *Then* `Laps.db` SHALL contain exactly 2 lap records (Lap 1 = 10 min, Lap 2 = 15 min), and zero zero-duration laps.<br>• *Given* an attempt to invoke `LapsDatabaseManager.saveLap()` with `lapTime = 0` and `lapDistance = 0.0`,<br>• *Then* the method SHALL discard the write and log a warning without inserting into `Laps.TABLE`.<br>• *Given* a database containing a historical zero-duration lap from prior app versions,<br>• *When* `LapsDatabaseManager.getLaps(workoutId)` is queried,<br>• *Then* the zero-duration lap SHALL be excluded from the returned list.<br><br>**Invariants**: Manual lap splitting (`TrackingViewsRepository`, `PebbleService`), total active time/distance calculation (`REQ-TRK-001`), live pause duration updates (`REQ-UI-038`), and TCX/GPX export schema compliance (`REQ-DAT-012`) MUST NOT be broken. | Eliminate confusing phantom zero-duration laps from workout summaries, preserve Rabbit/Hedgehog performance badge integrity, and ensure clean TCX exports by aligning pause/resume behavior with standard athletic tracking. | `TrainingApplication.java`, `TrackerService.java`, `LapsDatabaseManager.java` | `TST-TRK-002` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-003** | Use WakeLocks during active tracking. | Prevent CPU sleep and data gaps. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-REG-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-004** | Automatically guess Sport Type and Equipment. | Minimize user effort via automated categorization. | `EquipmentDiscoveryManager.kt` | `TST-UNT-003` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-005** | Implement session recovery ("Resume from Crash"). | Ensure data integrity against system pressure. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-STR-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-006** | Support sport-specific search triggers. | Sensors ready when user changes activity. | `TrainingApplication.java` | `TST-MAN-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-007** | Deterministic 1Hz sampling rate during recording. | Consistent time-base for analysis and export. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-REG-001` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-008** | Align session averages with core summary metrics. | Ensure background tracking focus matches optimized UI summary for consistency and performance. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-STR-004` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-009** | Total Time Persistence. | The `TrackerService` SHALL continue to update the `TIME_TOTAL_s` field in the `WorkoutSummaries` database table even when the recording is in a PAUSED state. | `TrackerService.java` | `TST-REG-007` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-010** | **Live Tracking Finalization Event Dispatch.** | Upon tracking completion (`endWorkout`), the system SHALL broadcast `WORKOUT_UPDATED_INTENT` and `TRACKING_FINISHED_INTENT` with the workout ID parameter (`WORKOUT_ID`) via `LocalBroadcastManager`, while preserving the package-targeted system broadcast of `TRACKING_FINISHED_INTENT`. The system SHALL ensure downstream subscribers (`WorkoutRepository`, `PeriodsRepository`, `WorkoutClusterEngine`) consume the finalized session to reactively create and update period summaries (Day, Week, Month, Year).<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an active live tracking session,<br>• *When* the workout is finished,<br>• *Then* `LocalBroadcastManager` SHALL dispatch `WORKOUT_UPDATED_INTENT` with extra `WORKOUT_ID` = `mWorkoutID`, triggering atomic rollup in `PeriodsRepository`.<br>**Invariants**: Existing intent action names and extras MUST NOT be changed; system-level broadcast receivers (`TrainingApplication`, `MainActivityWithNavigation`) MUST NOT be disrupted. | Ensure live-tracked workouts immediately generate and update period summaries, matching the reactive behavior of TCX imports. | `TrackerService.java`, `WorkoutRepository.kt`, `PeriodsRepository.kt` | `TST-PER-016` | Verified |
| **REQ-TRK-011** | **Intelligent Workout Auto-Naming based on Recognized Start and Destination Lieblingsorte.** | The system SHALL automatically generate meaningful, localized workout names based on recognized favorite locations (*Lieblingsorte*) for recorded sessions that do not match an existing Route Cluster (ATT-1398):<br>1. *Start & Destination Location Resolution*:<br>• Upon workout finalization in `TrackerService.java`, when a session does not match an existing cluster (`suggestion == null`), the system SHALL resolve start and end coordinates (`startPosRaw`, `endPosRaw`) against `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.getMyLocation(...)`.<br>2. *Naming Heuristics*:<br>• *Round Trips (Start == Destination within geofence)*: When both start and end resolve to the same location (or $\le \text{geofence radius}$), the name SHALL format based on activity sport type:<br>  - Running (`BSportType.RUN`): Localized \"Run from %1$s\" (e.g. German: \"Lauf ab %1$s\").<br>  - Cycling (`BSportType.BIKE`): Localized \"Ride from %1$s\" (e.g. German: \"Fahrt ab %1$s\").<br>  - General / Other (`BSportType.UNKNOWN` / `CONFLICT`): Localized \"Loop from %1$s\" (e.g. German: \"Runde ab %1$s\").<br>• *Point-to-Point (Start != Destination, both recognized)*: When start and destination resolve to distinct locations:<br>  - Running: Localized \"Run from %1$s to %2$s\" (German: \"Lauf von %1$s nach %2$s\").<br>  - Cycling: Localized \"Ride from %1$s to %2$s\" (German: \"Fahrt von %1$s nach %2$s\").<br>  - Other: Localized \"Activity from %1$s to %2$s\" (German: \"Aktivität von %1$s nach %2$s\").<br>• *Start Only Recognized*: When only start resolves to a known location, format with single-location prefix (e.g. \"Run from %1$s\" / \"Lauf ab %1$s\").<br>• *Destination Only Recognized*: When only destination resolves, format as \"Run to %1$s\" / \"Lauf nach %1$s\".<br>• *Neither Recognized (Fallback)*: If neither start nor destination matches a known location, the system SHALL retain standard default naming (`mBaseFileName`).<br>3. *Cluster Proposal Seeding (`WorkoutClusterEngine.kt`)*:<br>• When suggesting or creating a new Route Cluster for an unclustered track that starts at a known location, the default cluster name SHALL be seeded with \"Loop from %1$s\" / \"Runde ab %1$s\" instead of generic \"Workout at YYYY-MM-DD\".<br>4. *User Sovereignty & Invariants*:<br>• Established route cluster matches (`suggestion != null`) SHALL take precedence over location naming.<br>• Manual user edits to workout names (`WorkoutRepository.setWorkoutName`) SHALL remain strictly immutable.<br>• Single-thread database serialization (`KnownLocationsDB-Thread`), hardware sport type inference, and 9-language localization parity SHALL be preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an unclustered run recorded from \"Zuhause\" returning to \"Zuhause\",<br>• *When* the workout is finalized,<br>• *Then* `WORKOUT_NAME` in SQLite SHALL be set to \"Lauf ab Zuhause\" (in German) or \"Run from Zuhause\" (in English).<br>• *Given* an unclustered bike ride from \"Zuhause\" to \"Büro\",<br>• *When* finalized,<br>• *Then* `WORKOUT_NAME` SHALL be set to \"Fahrt von Zuhause nach Büro\" (DE) or \"Ride from Zuhause to Büro\" (EN).<br>• *Given* a workout matching an existing cluster \"Isarrunde #5\",<br>• *When* finalized,<br>• *Then* the cluster name \"Isarrunde #5\" SHALL take precedence over location auto-naming.<br>• *Given* an unclustered workout in a wilderness area with no known locations,<br>• *When* finalized,<br>• *Then* the standard base file name fallback SHALL be retained.<br><br>**Invariants**: Cluster naming priority, user manual edit immutability, hardware sport type inference, and 9-language localization parity MUST NOT be broken. | Provide meaningful automatic workout names for unclustered activities using recognized start and destination locations, eliminating manual rename friction in the app and Strava. | `TrackerService.java`, `WorkoutAutoNamingHelper.kt`, `WorkoutClusterEngine.kt`, `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java` | `TST-TRK-003` | Verified |

| **REQ-SET-052** | **Modal Display Settings & Synchronized Preference State.** | The system SHALL provide direct access to display-related preferences (`forcePortrait`, `keepScreenOn`, `noUnlocking`) via a modal dialog (`DisplaySettingsDialog`) triggered from the navigation drawer (`DisplaySettingsDialogFragment`):<br>1. *Default State Synchronization*: The display settings dialog MUST initialize switch states using `TrainingApplication.DEFAULT_DISPLAY_OPTIONS` (with `forcePortrait`, `keepScreenOn`, and `noUnlocking` all enabled) whenever the preference key `pref_display_options` is not explicitly persisted in `SharedPreferences`. The visual switch state in the dialog MUST match the runtime evaluation of `TrainingApplication.forcePortrait()`, `TrainingApplication.keepScreenOn()`, and `TrainingApplication.NoUnlocking()`.<br>2. *Atomic State Hoisting*: The dialog state MUST be hoisted at the dialog root to ensure toggling any display switch atomically updates the option set and persists it to `SharedPreferences` without dropping or reverting toggles made to sibling switches.<br>3. *Bidirectional Dynamic Window & Orientation Application*: When display options are modified or the dialog is dismissed, the host activity (`MainActivityWithNavigation`) SHALL immediately and dynamically apply the settings:<br>• `keepScreenOn`: Sets `window.decorView.keepScreenOn` to the matching boolean value.<br>• `noUnlocking`: When enabled, adds `WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SHOW_WHEN_LOCKED`; when disabled, explicitly clears `FLAG_SHOW_WHEN_LOCKED`.<br>• `forcePortrait`: When enabled, sets `requestedOrientation = ActivityInfo.SCREEN_ORIENTATION_PORTRAIT`; when disabled, explicitly resets `requestedOrientation = ActivityInfo.SCREEN_ORIENTATION_UNSPECIFIED`.<br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a fresh install or an environment where `pref_display_options` has not been modified,<br>• *When* the user opens the Display Settings dialog from the navigation drawer,<br>• *Then* all three switches ("force portrait", "keep screen on", "keep screen unlocked") SHALL be displayed in the ON (checked) state.<br>• *Given* the Display Settings dialog,<br>• *When* the user toggles "keep screen on" to OFF and then toggles "keep screen unlocked" to OFF,<br>• *Then* both settings SHALL remain OFF, and SharedPreferences SHALL contain only `["forcePortrait"]`.<br>• *When* the user disables "force portrait",<br>• *Then* the activity orientation lock SHALL be released (`SCREEN_ORIENTATION_UNSPECIFIED`) dynamically without requiring an activity restart.<br>**Invariants**: The SharedPreferences key `pref_display_options`, option string literals (`forcePortrait`, `keepScreenOn`, `noUnlocking`), and backward-compatible reading of existing user preferences MUST NOT change. | `DisplaySettingsDialog.kt`, `DisplaySettingsDialogFragment.kt`, `MainActivityWithNavigation.kt`, `TrainingApplication.java` | `TST-NAV-004` | Verified |

Instead, the system SHALL extract only the athlete's own achievements and serialize a compact JSON payload (`"v": 2`) containing strictly `id`, `segment_efforts` (`name`, `elapsed_time`, `pr_rank`, `kom_rank`, `starred`, `segment_id`), and `best_efforts` (`name`, `elapsed_time`, `pr_rank`, `distance`). All extraneous fields (kudos, comments, athlete profiles, photos, external URLs, polyline vectors) SHALL be discarded before storage.<br>2. *Deterministic Omission of Null/Absent Fields*: In the minimized schema (`"v": 2`), optional fields that are null, empty, non-positive, or false (e.g. unranked efforts, unstarred segments, zero distances) SHALL be omitted from serialization rather than written as explicit JSON nulls.<br>3. *Strict Command-Query Separation (Zero Write-on-Read)*: `StravaUploadDbHelper.getStravaActivityData()` and related query methods SHALL remain strictly read-only and MUST NOT perform implicit write operations, row updates, or database mutations during cursor reads.<br>4. *Robustness & Truncation Resilience*: `StravaActivityParser.parse()` SHALL handle both legacy uncompacted JSON (v1) and minimized JSON (v2) transparently. If a payload is truncated, corrupted, or malformed, the parser SHALL catch `JSONException`, log a warning, and safely return `null` without throwing unhandled runtime exceptions.<br>5. *System Invariants*:<br>• In-memory duplicate reconciliation and segment PR extraction (`processSegmentEffortsForPrs`) in `StravaUploader` SHALL continue to execute on the full in-memory response prior to storage.<br>• Offline rendering in `StravaActivitySection` (celebration banners, best efforts, segment accordions) SHALL retain 100% visual and functional parity.<br>• `StravaDataPurgeManager.purgeAllStravaData()` SHALL continue to wipe all local records on deauthorization.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a raw Strava activity response containing kudos, athlete profile, photos, comments, and segment efforts,<br>• *When* `StravaActivityParser.minimize(...)` or `StravaUploader.doUpdate` processes the payload,<br>• *Then* the persisted JSON SHALL contain `"v": 2`, athlete achievements (`segment_efforts`, `best_efforts`), and SHALL NOT contain athlete profile or social engagement fields.<br>• *Given* a segment effort with no PR (`pr_rank == null`),<br>• *When* serialized to minimized JSON,<br>• *Then* `"pr_rank"` SHALL be omitted from the effort JSON object.<br>• *Given* a truncated or malformed JSON string stored in SQLite,<br>• *When* `StravaActivityParser.parse()` executes,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `null` safely without crashing the UI thread.<br>• *Given* any read invocation of `StravaUploadDbHelper.getStravaActivityData()`,<br>• *When* executed,<br>• *Then* zero database write transactions or row updates SHALL be executed. | Comply with Strava API Agreement Section 6.2 (Cache & Retention), eliminate database bloat, and protect UI thread stability via strict CQS. | `StravaActivityData.kt`, `StravaUploader.kt`, `StravaUploadDbHelper.java`, `StravaActivitySection.kt` | `TST-EXP-010` | Verified |

Deletion Obligation & Section 6.2 Cache and Retention) regarding authorization termination, while protecting native athlete data and hardware sensor configurations:<br>1. *Mandatory Purge on Deauthorization & Revocation*: Upon explicit user disconnection in `StravaSettingsDialog` or automated server-side revocation detection (unrecoverable token refresh failure with `invalid_grant` / HTTP 400 in `StravaHelper.getRefreshedAccessToken`), the system SHALL execute a comprehensive data purge:<br>• *Credentials & State*: Remove all Strava tokens (`SP_STRAVA_TOKEN`, `SP_STRAVA_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `SP_STRAVA_TOKEN_EXPIRES_AT`, `SP_STRAVA_ATHLETE_ID`) and reset Strava upload toggles (`SP_UPLOAD_TO_STRAVA`) and demo mode to `false` in `SharedPreferences`.<br>• *Activity Details*: Purge all Strava activity JSON data, segment efforts, best efforts, PR/KOM rankings, and Strava activity IDs (`STRAVA_ACTIVITY_DATA` and `STRAVA_ID`) from `StravaUploadDbHelper` (`StravaUpload.db`).<br>• *Starred Segments*: Delete all Strava starred segments from `SegmentsDatabaseManager` (`Segments.db`) and clear in-memory cache in `SegmentsRepository`.<br>• *Strava Routes*: Delete all routes originating from Strava (`ORIGIN = 'STRAVA'` / Strava route IDs) from `RoutesDatabaseManager` (`Routes.db`) and refresh in-memory cache in `RoutesRepository`.<br>• *Equipment Unlinking*: In `EquipmentDbHelper` (`Equipment.db`), clear `StravaId = NULL` and `StravaName = NULL` across all equipment items, preserving local equipment entities, hardware sensor pairings (ANT+/BLE in `Links` table), and sport type links.<br>• *Worker Cancellation*: Cancel automated periodic synchronization workers (`StravaSegmentsSyncWorker` and `StravaRoutesSyncWorker`) via Android `WorkManager`.<br>• *UI State Notification*: Update the UI state across the application to reflect the disconnected state (`isConnected = false`).<br>2. *Remote Deauthorization*: When initiated by the user, the deauthorization request to Strava (`/oauth/deauthorize`) SHALL be dispatched using modern `OkHttpClient` before local credentials are wiped. If network fails, local data purging MUST still proceed.<br>3. *Automated Revocation Detection*: When `StravaHelper.getRefreshedAccessToken()` encounters an unrecoverable OAuth error (`invalid_grant` / HTTP 400), it SHALL automatically trigger the local data purge.<br>4. *Reauthorization Integrity & Deduplication*: Upon subsequent reauthorization (`StravaAuthState.Success`), `StravaEquipmentSynchronizeThread` SHALL match unlinked local equipment by `Name` where `StravaId IS NULL`, restoring `StravaId` and `StravaName` without creating duplicate equipment rows. Starred segments and routes SHALL be freshly synchronized without creating duplicate route or segment rows across concurrent sync tasks or repeated reconnects: `RoutesRepository.syncRoutesFromStrava` and `SegmentsRepository.syncStarredSegments` SHALL serialize concurrent sync executions with a `Mutex`, `RoutesDatabaseManager.insertRoute` and `SegmentsDatabaseManager.addOrUpdateSegment` SHALL idempotently update existing records and purge legacy duplicate rows when matching external/Strava IDs, `SegmentsDatabaseManager.insertSegmentStreams` SHALL delete existing stream records before re-inserting points, `SegmentsDatabaseManager.getAllSegmentSummaries` SHALL filter duplicates in-memory, `SegmentsRepository._allSegmentsWithPath` SHALL update existing segments in-place, and `StravaSettingsDialog` SHALL execute segment synchronization sequentially rather than dispatching concurrent `BIKE` and `RUN` sync jobs.<br>5. *Interactive Disconnect Confirmation*: When an athlete initiates disconnection in `StravaSettingsDialog`, the system SHALL NOT immediately purge data or deauthorize. It SHALL present a modal confirmation dialog clearly detailing the consequences (deletion of Strava routes, starred segments and times, unlinking of equipment from Strava, and removal of Strava upload status for past workouts) and reassuring the user that native recorded workouts remain untouched. Disconnection and data purging SHALL ONLY proceed upon explicit confirmation, and all dialog strings SHALL be localized across all 9 supported languages.<br>6. *Invariants*: Native workout sessions, GPS trackpoint streams in `WorkoutSamplesDatabaseManager`, calculated metrics and durations in `WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager`, and interval records in `LapsDatabaseManager` recorded natively by aTrainingTracker MUST NOT be deleted. Non-Strava local routes, local equipment hardware bindings, and sport types MUST remain completely intact. | Comply with Strava API Policy Section 7.4 mandating permanent deletion of Strava data upon token revocation, while protecting native athlete workout recordings and hardware sensor links. | `StravaAuthManager.kt`, `StravaSettingsDialog.kt`, `StravaDeauthorizationThread.java`, `StravaDataPurgeManager.kt`, `StravaHelper.kt`, `TrainingApplication.java`, `StravaUploadDbHelper.java`, `SegmentsDatabaseManager.java`, `SegmentsRepository.kt`, `RoutesDatabaseManager.kt`, `RoutesRepository.kt`, `EquipmentDbHelper.java` | `TST-EXT-006` | Verified |
| **REQ-EXT-010** | **Strava Route & Segment 7-Day TTL Cache Retention, Orphan Pruning & Route Preservation.** | The system SHALL enforce strict compliance with Section 6.2 ("Cache and Retention") of the Strava API Agreement and Developer Terms across all Strava-originated routes and starred segments:<br>1. *7-Day Retention Limit & Persistent Timestamping*: The system SHALL NOT retain cached Strava routes (`RouteSource.STRAVA` in `Routes.db`) or starred segments (in `Segments.db`) for longer than 7 days (604,800,000 ms) without fresh synchronization. Both `Routes.db` (`TABLE_ROUTES`) and `Segments.db` (`TABLE_STARRED_SEGMENTS`) SHALL maintain a `synced_at` timestamp column (`INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, Schema v8). Whenever a route or segment is synchronized or updated from the Strava API, its `synced_at` timestamp SHALL be updated to current epoch milliseconds (`System.currentTimeMillis()`).<br>2. *Automated TTL Expiration & Cascade Eviction*: The system SHALL automatically evict records where `currentTimeMillis() - synced_at > 7 days`. TTL eviction SHALL execute upon repository instantiation (`init`), during background sync worker execution (`StravaRoutesSyncWorker`, `StravaSegmentsSyncWorker`), and on demand. For expired segments, the eviction SHALL cascade-delete associated polyline stream coordinates from `SegmentStreamsTable`.<br>3. *Orphan & Tombstone Pruning*: During remote synchronization, the system SHALL compare local Strava records against the remote API response. Any local route with `source == RouteSource.STRAVA` whose external Strava ID is absent from the active remote route set SHALL be promptly pruned from `Routes.db`. Similarly, any local starred segment whose Strava ID is absent from the active remote starred segments set SHALL be pruned from `Segments.db` alongside its stream coordinates.<br>4. *Athlete Route Preservation (Local GPX Duplication)*: To allow athletes to retain desired navigation tracks permanently offline without violating Strava caching limits, the system SHALL provide a "Save as Local Route" / "Als lokale Route speichern" feature. Duplicating a Strava route SHALL create an independent route record in `Routes.db` with `source = RouteSource.LOCAL_GPX`, clear external Strava identifiers, and copy all spatial coordinate points, bounds, and elevation profiles. Converted local routes SHALL be athlete-owned data and SHALL NOT be subject to Strava TTL eviction or orphan pruning.<br>5. *System Invariants*: Native recorded workouts (`WorkoutSummaries.db`, `WorkoutSamples.db`, `Laps.db`), athlete-owned routes (`RouteSource.LOCAL_GPX` and `RouteSource.WORKOUT`), recurring route clusters in `WorkoutCluster.db`, and hardware sensor bindings in `Equipment.db` MUST NOT be touched, altered, or deleted during TTL eviction or orphan pruning. Eviction operations MUST execute safely in background transactions without blocking UI threads or failing on offline devices. | Comply with Strava API Agreement Section 6.2 mandating a 7-day maximum cache retention and prompt orphan deletion, while safeguarding athlete-owned routes, native workout records, and sensor configurations. | `RoutesDatabaseManager.kt`, `RoutesRepository.kt`, `SegmentsDatabaseManager.java`, `SegmentsRepository.kt`, `StravaRoutesSyncWorker.kt`, `StravaSegmentsSyncWorker.kt` | `TST-EXT-007` | Verified |

| **REQ-CON-016** | **Smartphone Battery Remaining Duration Continuous Countdown & Discrete Transition Drain Rate Architecture.** | The system SHALL compute smartphone battery drain rate strictly across discrete percentage step-down transition events and provide a continuous, monotonic countdown during periods of constant battery level, eliminating sampling-induced upward drift and abrupt multi-hour estimate plunges (ATT-1631):<br>1. *Discrete Transition-Triggered Drain Rate Computation (`BatteryDevice.java`)*:<br>• The system SHALL record discrete battery percentage transition points: `BatteryStep(int activeSeconds, int percent)`.<br>• Baseline initialization: At workout start or accumulator reset, record `(mActiveRecordingSeconds, mBatteryLevel)`.<br>• Step-down recording: A new `BatteryStep` SHALL be recorded strictly when `mBatteryLevel < lastRecordedStep.percent`.<br>• Drain rate evaluation: When evaluating drain rate, the system SHALL calculate the rate between the oldest step in the rolling window ($t_0, P_0$) and the latest step ($t_k, P_k$): $\Delta t = t_k - t_0$, $\Delta P = P_0 - P_k$, $\text{drainRatePerHour} = \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t / 3600.0}$. When $\Delta t \ge \text{MIN\_STABILIZATION\_SECONDS}$ (300s) and $\Delta P \ge 1$, update `mEstablishedDrainRatePerHour = drainRatePerHour`, `mBaseRemainingSeconds = round((mBatteryLevel / drainRatePerHour) * 3600.0)`, and `mLastStepActiveSeconds = t_k`.<br>2. *Continuous Monotonic Countdown Between Step Transitions*:<br>• During active recording while the battery percentage remains constant ($t > mLastStepActiveSeconds$), remaining seconds SHALL count down: $\text{elapsedSinceStep} = mActiveRecordingSeconds - mLastStepActiveSeconds$, $\text{remainingSeconds} = mBaseRemainingSeconds - elapsedSinceStep$.<br>• *Monotonicity Invariant*: Remaining duration SHALL NEVER increase or drift upwards while battery percentage is constant.<br>• *Lower Bound Floor Clamping*: Remaining seconds SHALL be clamped to the floor of $(P - 1)$: $\text{floorSeconds} = \text{round}(((mBatteryLevel - 1) / mEstablishedDrainRatePerHour) * 3600.0)$, $\text{remainingSeconds} = \max(\text{floorSeconds}, \text{remainingSeconds})$, $\text{remainingSeconds} = \max(0, \text{remainingSeconds})$.<br>3. *Warmup & Stabilization*:<br>• The sensor SHALL emit `BatteryRemainingTimeFormatter.STABILIZING_STATUS_CODE` (`-2`, formatting as `--:--`) until active recording time reaches $\ge 300\text{s}$ AND a drop of $\ge 1\%$ is measured.<br>• If a 1% drop occurs prior to 300s, stabilization completes once total active recording reaches 300s using the effective elapsed time.<br>4. *Charging & Pause Invariants*:<br>• When connected to charger (`mIsCharging == true`), the sensor emits `CHARGING_STATUS_CODE` (`-1`).<br>• When tracking is paused, `mActiveRecordingSeconds` does not increment, preserving countdown state without drift.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: `REQ-CON-015` (*Smartphone Battery Level and Estimated Remaining Duration Telemetry Sensors*), targeting `BatteryDevice.java`.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `809bc479` (Ticket `ATT-1454`, Sprint `2026-40.4`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ATT-1454` added periodic 30s samples to estimate drain rate, not anticipating that discrete 1% quantization causes time $\Delta t$ to increase while $\Delta P$ is frozen at an integer, driving projected remaining time artificially upward.<br>4. *Refinement Reason*: On-road endurance testing demonstrated that constant battery levels caused remaining time to climb by several hours, followed by a violent downward jump upon the next 1% drop. Transition-based rate calculation combined with intra-step countdown restores accurate physical behavior.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: 1Hz sensor dispatch, zero wake-locks, zero disk I/O, `PHONE_BATTERY` accuracy, and charging detection remain 100% intact.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active workout tracking session where a battery drop has established a drain rate (e.g. 5.0%/h at 80%),<br>• *When* the battery level remains at 80% for several subsequent minutes,<br>• *Then* `BATTERY_REMAINING_TIME` SHALL count down steadily (decreasing second-by-second) and SHALL NEVER increase.<br>• *Given* an established drain rate and countdown at level $N$,<br>• *When* the battery level transitions from $N$ to $N - 1$,<br>• *Then* the new drain rate computed from the transition window SHALL smoothly adjust without erratic multi-hour jumps.<br>• *Given* active tracking in the first 300 seconds without confirmed drop,<br>• *When* `BATTERY_REMAINING_TIME` is queried,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `STABILIZING_STATUS_CODE` (`--:--`).<br>• *Given* an established drain rate of 10%/h (expected 360s per 1%),<br>• *When* active recording extends past 360s at the same percentage (e.g. 600s),<br>• *Then* remaining seconds SHALL NOT count down below the $(P - 1)$ threshold.<br><br>**Invariants**: PHONE_BATTERY reporting (0–100%), charging status detection, 1Hz telemetry dispatch, and zero wake-lock/disk-I/O invariants MUST NOT be broken. | Compute battery drain rate strictly across discrete percentage step-down events and provide a continuous monotonic countdown while percentage is constant, eliminating upward drift and abrupt jumps. | `BatteryDevice.java` | `TST-CON-007` | Verified |

| **REQ-DAT-014** | **Internet Digital Elevation Model (DEM) Reference Altitude Retrieval, Spatial Caching & Legacy Location Healing.** | The system SHALL retrieve topographic ground-truth elevation from an open Digital Elevation Model (DEM) service over the internet to calibrate barometric altitude sensors at workout start points:<br>1. *Authoritative DEM Retrieval*: When establishing a reference altitude for a workout start location, the system SHALL query the Open-Meteo Elevation API (`https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/elevation?latitude={lat}&longitude={lng}`) asynchronously via `ElevationService` on a background I/O dispatcher (`Dispatchers.IO`) without blocking the sensor dispatch thread or UI Looper.<br>2. *Coordinate Quantization*: Latitude and longitude parameters submitted to the elevation API and persisted in `StartLocation2Altitude.db` SHALL be rounded to 5 decimal places ($\approx 1.1\text{m}$ precision at the equator) to eliminate microscopic GPS jitter.<br>3. *Spatial Geofence Caching*: The system SHALL utilize a spatial distance query against the configured location radius ($200\text{m}$). Any workout starting within the radius of an existing cached entry SHALL reuse the stored altitude and MUST NOT trigger redundant network requests.<br>4. *Database Schema Evolution (V4 to V5)*: In `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java`, `StartLocation2Altitude.db` SHALL be upgraded to `DB_VERSION = 5` adding columns `is_locked INTEGER DEFAULT 0` and `source TEXT DEFAULT 'LEGACY_RAW'`. All migrations MUST adhere to `REQ-DAT-008` (atomic framework transactions without manual transaction handling).<br>5. *Locked Location Immutability Invariant*: Any database entry where `is_locked == 1` MUST be strictly immutable against automated mutations, refinements, or overwrites.<br>6. *Fault Resilience & Offline Degradation*: The HTTP client MUST enforce a 5-second connection/read timeout. Upon HTTP 429 (rate limit) or 503/5xx (server error) or network absence (offline), the system SHALL degrade gracefully to GPS altitude (persisting with `source = GPS_FALLBACK` and `is_locked = 0`) and trip a circuit breaker to prevent battery or socket exhaustion.<br>7. *Legacy Location Migration & Asynchronous Batch Healing*: During V4 to V5 migration, all existing records SHALL be initialized with `is_locked = 0` and `source = 'LEGACY_RAW'`. When online connectivity is available, the system SHALL execute an asynchronous batch DEM elevation query for all unlocked legacy records, atomically updating their stored altitudes to ground-truth DEM values and transitioning their source to `'INTERNET_DEM'`. If any legacy location has `is_locked == 1`, it MUST NOT be altered.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an active internet connection and a new workout start coordinate (lat 52.52000, lng 13.41000),<br>• *When* `ElevationService.fetchElevation()` is invoked,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL parse the response (`elevation[0]`), persist the record with `source = INTERNET_DEM`, and apply the elevation to `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.setAltitudeCorrection()`.<br>• *Given* a location already present in `StartLocation2Altitude.db` within 200m,<br>• *When* tracking starts,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL use the cached altitude immediately with zero network requests.<br>• *Given* existing legacy records in V4 upon upgrade to V5,<br>• *When* online connectivity is established,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL query Open-Meteo in batch, update all unlocked legacy records with DEM elevations, and set `source = INTERNET_DEM`.<br>• *Given* a location with `is_locked == 1`,<br>• *When* automated learning or batch healing runs,<br>• *Then* the stored altitude and metadata SHALL remain unchanged.<br>• *Given* the device is offline or the request times out after 5 seconds,<br>• *When* elevation is queried,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL fall back to GPS altitude without crashing or blocking the sensor thread.<br><br>**Invariants**: Cold-start baseline protection (`REQ-CON-011`), null-safe correction dispatch (`REQ-CON-013`), atomic database upgrade transactions (`REQ-DAT-008`), and downstream sample shifts (`REQ-FIL-004`) MUST NOT be altered or regressed. | Eliminate weather-induced barometric calibration drift by providing authoritative ground-truth elevation from internet DEM datasets with spatial caching, offline resilience, and automatic healing of legacy locations. | `ElevationService.kt`, `ElevationSource.kt`, `KnownLocationsDatabaseManager.java`, `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.java` | `TST-DAT-008` | Verified |

reference altitudes through running averages.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ATT-1366` placed `learnLocation(..., ExtremaType.START)` inside `initPressureSensor()` under the assumption (`setAltitudeCorrection`), and `hitCount` in `StartLocation2Altitude.db` SHALL remain strictly 5.<br>• *Given* an existing known location with `hitCount = 5`,<br>• *When* the user starts a new workout | **REQ-UI-130** | **Sport-Specific Equipment Selection & In-Place Expansion in Edit Workout Dialog.** | Within the workout editing dialog (`EditWorkoutScreen` / `EditWorkoutViewModel`), the system SHALL strictly partition available equipment options by the active workout's base sport type (`currentBSportType`):<br>1. *Base Sport Type Partitioning (`BSportType` Firewall)*:<br>• For `BSportType.BIKE`: Available equipment SHALL be constrained strictly to bicycles (`frameType` $\in 1..4$, `sportType == BIKE`). Selecting the expansion item SHALL expand the dropdown options list in-place (via `stayOpenOn`) to display `- none -` and all equipment belonging to that base sport ($A$).<br>• **Case 2 ($N == 1$: Exactly one equipment item linked to the sport)**: The dropdown options list SHALL present: `- none -` and all equipment of that base sport ($A$). The uniquely linked equipment item SHALL be automatically preselected.<br>• **Case 3 ($N == 0$: No equipment items linked to the sport)**: The dropdown options list SHALL present: `- none -` and all equipment of that base sport ($A$). `- none -` SHALL be preselected (unless the workout already has an assigned equipment item that is valid for this sport).<br>3. *Cross-Sport Switching Invariants*:<br>• When the user changes the sport type to a different `BSportType` (e.g. Cycling $\rightarrow$ Running): Any previously selected equipment item SHALL be cleared (since bicycles cannot be assigned to running workouts). otherwise, if the current equipment is valid for the base sport, it SHALL be retained.<br>4. *Cross-Sport Backdoor Elimination*:<br>• The generic token `+ all equipment +` and unfiltered fallback to `equipmentRepository.equipmentList` SHALL be eliminated from `EditWorkoutViewModel`, preventing cross-sport gear pollution.<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* a cycling workout with 2 linked bikes (Bike A, Bike B) and 1 unlinked bike (Bike C),<br>• *When* the equipment dropdown is opened,<br>• *Then* options SHALL be `[- none -, Bike A, Bike B, + all bikes +]`.<br>• *When* `+ all bikes +` is tapped,<br>• *Then* options SHALL expand in-place to `[- none -, Bike A, Bike B, Bike C]`, with zero running shoes displayed.<br>• *Given* a running workout with 1 linked shoe (Shoe 1) and 2 unlinked shoes (Shoe 2, Shoe 3),<br>• *When* the dialog opens,<br>• *Then* options SHALL be `[- none -, Shoe 1, Shoe 2, Shoe 3]` and `Shoe 1` SHALL be preselected.<br>• *Given* a cycling workout with 0 linked bikes,<br>• *When* the dialog opens for a new/unassigned workout,<br>• *Then* options SHALL be `[- none -, <all bikes>]` and `- none -` SHALL be preselected.<br>• *Given* an active workout with Bike A selected,<br>• *When* the user changes the sport to Running,<br>• *Then* the selected equipment SHALL NOT remain Bike A, but SHALL switch to the linked shoe ($N == 1$) or `- none -` ($N == 0$).<br>**Invariants**: `SportTypeEquipmentLinkManager` and `EquipmentDbHelper` data persistence MUST NOT be altered; | **REQ-UI-139** | **Right-Aligned Edge FastScrollbar, Isolated Thumb Touch Target & Continuous Drag Accumulation.** | The system SHALL position the fast scrollbar (`FastScrollbar.kt`) flush against the right edge of the viewport, isolate drag gesture detection strictly to the draggable thumb, and maintain continuous drag displacement accumulation:<br>1. *Flush Edge Alignment*: In `WorkoutList.kt`, `FastScrollbar` SHALL be aligned flush to `Alignment.CenterEnd` with zero end padding (`padding(end = 0.dp)`), eliminating floating inward offsets.<br>2. *Right-Aligned Track & Ergonomic Thumb*: In `FastScrollbar.kt`, the track (`width = 4.dp`) SHALL be aligned to `Alignment.CenterEnd` flush against the viewport edge. The draggable thumb hit box SHALL be aligned to `Alignment.TopEnd` with an ergonomic touch target (`width = 28.dp`, `height = 48.dp`) containing an 8dp visual pill aligned to `Alignment.CenterEnd`, ensuring effortless grabbing while physically isolating the track from list cards (which end at `screenWidth - 8.dp`).<br>3. *Isolated Thumb Touch Target & Gesture Scoping*: Drag gesture detection (`detectDragGestures`) SHALL be scoped strictly to the draggable thumb composable, and MUST NOT be declared on the full-height outer container Box. The track area above and below the thumb SHALL NOT capture or consume pointer input, ensuring underlying list item action buttons (e.g. 3-dots export menu, edit button) receive click events without interference.<br>4. *Continuous Drag Accumulation & Zero-Latency Visual Tracking*: During drag gestures, the scrollbar SHALL maintain an active drag state (`isDragging: Boolean`, `dragProgress: Float`), continuously accumulating fractional displacement deltas without per-frame integer truncation loss ($\text{dragProgress} = (\text{dragProgress} + \text{dragAmount.y} / \text{maxOffsetPx}).\text{coerceIn}(0f, 1f)$). The visual thumb position during dragging SHALL be driven directly by `dragProgress` for zero-lag responsiveness, while dispatching `state.scrollToItem(targetIndex)` across all items ($0 \dots \text{totalItems} - 1$).<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a scrollable list of workouts in `WorkoutList`,<br>• *When* the list is displayed,<br>• *Then* the fast scrollbar track and thumb SHALL sit flush against the right display edge.<br>• *Given* any list item card with right-aligned action buttons (such as the 3-dots menu or edit button in `WorkoutHeader`),<br>• *When* the user taps the button while the scrollbar thumb is at a different vertical position,<br>• *Then* the button click SHALL be triggered immediately and reliably without being intercepted by `FastScrollbar`.<br>• *Given* the fast scrollbar thumb,<br>• *When* the user touches and drags the thumb vertically at normal finger speed (small per-frame deltas),<br>• *Then* the thumb SHALL follow the finger with zero lag and the `LazyColumn` SHALL scroll smoothly across all items from first to last.<br><br>**Invariants**: Dynamic alpha fading (0.4f idle to 1.0f active scroll with 500ms tween), idle progress calculation from `firstVisibleItemIndex` / `firstVisibleItemScrollOffset`, and smooth scrolling via `scrollToItem` MUST NOT be regressed; list item layouts and action button callbacks MUST NOT be altered. | Eliminate click interception on right-aligned list actions while providing a responsive, edge-aligned fast scrollbar experience. | `FastScrollbar.kt`, `WorkoutList.kt` | `TST-UI-092` | Verified |

W_{\text{vis}}).coerceAtLeast(0.0)]$, preventing empty space panning beyond route start or termination.<br>3. *Instant Reset Affordances*:<br>• Double-tapping the graph surface SHALL immediately reset the profile to the full $1.0x$ view ($D_{\text{start}} = 0.0$, $Z = 1.0x$).<br>• When zoomed in ($Z > 1.0x$), the profile SHALL display an interactive overlay badge indicating the current zoom factor Commit Trace*: `ATT-508` (`calculateElevationBounds` outlier clamping and minimum 20m span) and `ElevationProfile.kt` initial Compose implementation.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ElevationProfile` originally hardcoded a static $0 .. \text{totalDist}$ mapping without visible window state or transform gesture processing.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Vertical bounds sanitization (`calculateElevationBounds`), grade percentage calculations (`TTColor.Zone1 .. Zone5`), adaptive canvas height (`calculateElevationProfileHeight`), and absolute distance metric dispatch (`onDistanceSelected`) MUST remain strictly intact.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an elevation profile displayed with route path points,<br>• *When* the athlete performs a horizontal pinch-to-zoom gesture (or taps the zoom-in button),<br>• *Then* the visible distance window SHALL scale accordingly (up to $10.0x$), expanding climbs and local terrain features horizontally.<br>• *Given* the elevation profile is in a zoomed-in state ($Z > 1.0x$),<br>• *When* the athlete drags horizontally,<br>• *Then* the profile SHALL pan across the distance axis, strictly clamped within $[0 .. D_{\text{total}}]$.<br>• *Given* the elevation profile is zoomed in,<br>• *When* the athlete double-taps the graph surface or taps the overlay reset button,<br>• *Then* the view SHALL immediately reset to the full $1.0x$ extent ($0 .. D_{\text{total}}$).<br>• *Given* the elevation profile is zoomed in,<br>• *When* the athlete scrubs along the visible curve,<br>• *Then* `onDistanceSelected` and the coordinate marker SHALL accurately reflect the absolute workout distance and elevation of the inspected point.<br><br>**Invariants**: Vertical elevation bounds, grade coloring thresholds, adaptive profile height, and absolute distance contract MUST NOT be altered. | Enable horizontal zoom and pan on the elevation profile chart with centroid scaling, double-tap reset, adaptive X-axis ticks, and synchronized coordinate scrubbing. | `ElevationProfile.kt` | `TST-UI-146` | Verified |

If `TIME_ACTIVE` and `TIME_TOTAL` are null, the repository SHALL fall back to deriving relative elapsed seconds from the `time` column ($t - t_0$), or sequential 1s intervals. `_uiState`.<br>5. *Visual UI Component (`HeartRateZoneDistributionCard.kt` & `ZoneDistributionColumnChart.kt`)*:<br>• The system SHALL render a 5-column vertical histogram with the 5 physiological heart rate zones (Zone 1 through Zone 5) on the X-axis and duration spent in each zone on the Y-axis.<br>• The column height for each zone SHALL be proportional to its duration relative to the maximum zone duration: $\text{heightFraction}_i = t_i / \max_j(t_j)$ (with a subtle minimum height of 4.dp for non-zero zones for visual visibility, and 0.dp for zero duration zones).<br>• Each vertical column SHALL be filled with its corresponding zone color `TTColor.Zone1` through `TTColor.Zone5`, with rounded top corners.<br>• Above/within each column, the system SHALL display formatted duration (`m:ss` or `h:mm:ss`) and percentage (`X%`).<br>• Below each column, the system SHALL display the zone label (`Z1`..`Z5`).<br>• The card SHALL display a compact title row with a heart icon (`R.drawable.ic_heart_rate`), localized text `R.string.aftermath_hr_zones_title`, and total active time.<br>6. *Slotted MapDetailLayout Integration (`MapDetailLayout.kt`, `TrackOnMapScreen.kt`)*:<br>• `MapDetailLayout` SHALL provide an optional `analyticsContent: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit = {}` slot directly integrated with the layout.<br>• If `hrZoneDistribution == null`, the component SHALL render nothing and consume 0 vertical space.<br>• For stationary / indoor workouts (`showMap == false`, `showElevationProfile == false`), `analyticsContent` SHALL remain fully visible.<br>7. *100% 9-Language Localization Parity*:<br>• `aftermath_hr_zones_title` SHALL be defined across all 9 supported locales (en, de, es, fr, it, ja, nl, pl, pt).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: REQ-UI-202 (*Aftermath: Heart Rate 5-Zone Distribution Bar Architecture*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-1389`, Sprint `2026-40.5`. Refined in ticket `ATT-1739`, Sprint `2026-40.6`, and `ATT-1811`, Sprint `2026-40.7`.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Originally formulated as a single horizontal stacked bar to minimize vertical card height. During Sprint Review 2026-40.5, user review rejected the stacked bar in favor of discrete vertical columns: 'The zones (Zone 1, Zone 2, .., Zone 5) must be on the x-Axis; the time in the corresponding Zone must be on the y-Axis.' | **REQ-UI-219** | **Aftermath/Graphs: Robust Running Pace Decoding, Stopped-Speed Clamping, and mm:ss Y-Axis Pace Formatting.** | The system SHALL enforce robust running pace decoding, stopped-speed clamping, and athletic mm:ss Y-axis label formatting across all Aftermath telemetry graphs and scrubbing cards (`ElevationProfile.kt`, `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`) (ATT-1818):<br>1. *ElevationProfile Scrubbing Pace Decoding & Stopped Clamping*:<br>• In `ElevationProfile.kt`, when `bSportType == BSportType.RUN`, the multi-metric scrubbing badge SHALL convert speed to seconds per meter ($s/m = 1.0 / point.speedMps$) and pass $s/m$ into `paceFormatter.format_with_units(1.0 / point.speedMps)`.<br>• When `point.speedMps == null || point.speedMps < 0.55` (speeds below 0.55 m/s / ~2.0 km/h, representing pauses or stops), the scrubbing badge SHALL invoke `paceFormatter.format_with_units(null)` to display `"-- min/km"` (or `"-- min/mile"` in Imperial), eliminating division-by-zero, infinity, and implausible walking paces.<br>• Non-running sports SHALL continue formatting speed via `speedFormatter.format_with_units(point.speedMps)` in `km/h` or `mph`.<br>2. *TelemetryMetricUtils Value Formatting (`TelemetryMetricUtils.formatValue`)*:<br>• For `TelemetryMetricType.PACE`, `formatValue` SHALL convert `value` (in minutes per unit) to seconds per meter ($s/m$): `spm = (value * 60.0) / metersPerUnit` (where `metersPerUnit` is 1000.0 for Metric and `BANALService.METER_PER_MILE` for Imperial) and pass $spm$ into `paceFormatter.format_with_units(spm)`. When `value == null`, it SHALL return `"--"`.<br>3. *Athletic Pace Y-Axis Formatting (`formatPaceMinutes` / `mm:ss`)*:<br>• `TelemetryMetricUtils` SHALL provide a public helper `formatPaceMinutes(paceMinutes: Double): String` returning `String.format(Locale.US, "%d:%02d", min, sec)`.<br>• In `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, when `metricType == TelemetryMetricType.PACE`, Y-axis maximum label (top / fastest, corresponding to `dataMin`) and minimum label (bottom / slowest, corresponding to `dataMax`) SHALL be rendered via `formatPaceMinutes(...)`. Raw decimal float formatting (`String.format(Locale.US, "%.1f", ...)`) SHALL NOT be used for Pace.<br>4. *Dynamic Range Bounding & Stopped Filtering (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• In `extractMetricValue` for `PACE`, speeds below $0.55 \text{ m/s}$ SHALL return `null` (treated as stopped/paused), and pace values SHALL be bounded within realistic athletic limits: coerced to `[1.5, 20.0]`.<br>• In `dataMin` and `dataMax` calculation for `PACE`, `dataMin` and `dataMax` SHALL be derived from active running points with a minimum spread of at least 1.0 min/km: `dataMin = (min * 0.95).coerceAtLeast(1.5)`, `dataMax = (max * 1.05).coerceAtMost(20.0)`, `dataMax = max(dataMax, dataMin + 1.0)`.<br>5. *Preservation of Core Invariants*:<br>• Pace inversion logic in `TelemetryMetricGraph` (faster pace near top, slower pace near bottom) remains strictly preserved.<br>• Synchronized multi-chart scrubbing via `selectedDistance` and global horizontal zoom alignment remain 100% intact.<br>• Non-running sports (cycling, hiking) remain unaffected and continue using `SpeedFormatter`.<br>• 100% 9-language localization parity is maintained.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-UI-219`), extending and refining `REQ-UI-206` under Epic `ATT-111` (*Compact Post-Workout Visual Analytics & Graphs*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `061a4b35` (`ATT-1740`) introduced `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` and initial pace conversion; ticket `ATT-1391` introduced multi-metric scrubbing.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `ElevationProfile.kt` passed speed (m/s) to `PaceFormatter` (which expects s/m), producing 69:27 min/km for a 15 km/h runner. Decimal labels (1.0, 33.0) and unconstrained pause samples distorted the chart.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: `PaceFormatter` s/m contract, metric and imperial unit parity, synchronized scrubbing, and localization parity are 100% strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete inspecting a running workout in `ElevationProfile`,<br>• *When* scrubbing at a point with speed 4.167 m/s (15 km/h),<br>• *Then* the scrubbing badge SHALL display `"4:00 min/km"` (Metric) or `"6:26 min/mile"` (Imperial), and SHALL NOT display `"69:27 min/km"`.<br>• *Given* an athlete scrubbing at a stopped point ($speedMps < 0.55\text{ m/s}$ or null),<br>• *When* rendered,<br>• *Then* the pace text SHALL render as `"-- min/km"` (or `"-- min/mile"`).<br>• *Given* `TelemetryMetricGraph` rendering a running workout (`metricType == PACE`),<br>• *When* inspecting Y-axis labels,<br>• *Then* top and bottom labels SHALL be formatted in athletic `mm:ss` format (e.g. `"4:00"`, `"6:00"`), and SHALL NOT display raw decimal numbers (`"1.0"`, `"33.0"`).<br>• *Given* a running workout with pause/stop points,<br>• *When* rendered in `TelemetryMetricGraph`,<br>• *Then* pause points SHALL NOT expand `dataMax` to 33.0, and the running curve SHALL utilize the vertical chart height effectively.<br><br>**Invariants**: Inverted pace plotting (faster higher), synchronized multi-chart scrubbing, SpeedFormatter usage for cycling/hiking, and 9-language localization parity MUST NOT be broken. | Enforce robust running pace decoding, stopped-speed clamping (<0.55 m/s to '-- min/km'), mm:ss Y-axis label formatting, and dynamic range bounding on Aftermath pace telemetry graphs and scrubbers. | `ElevationProfile.kt`, `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` | `TST-UI-173` | Verified |
| **REQ-UI-220** | **Aftermath/Graphs: Adaptive X-Axis Milestone Decimation, Collision Prevention, and Standardized Boundary Labeling.** | The system SHALL enforce adaptive X-axis milestone decimation, collision prevention, and boundary label parity across all Aftermath continuous telemetry graphs (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, `ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt`) (ATT-1819):<br>1. *Adaptive 2 km Step Progression (`ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt`)*:<br>• In `ElevationProfileZoomMath.calculateAdaptiveDistanceStep`, when `unit == MyUnits.METRIC`, the system SHALL provide an intermediate step for workouts with visible distance between 10 km and 20 km: `visibleDist > 10_000 -> 2_000f`. Workouts in `(10_000, 20_000]` meters SHALL generate 2,000m tick intervals rather than 1,000m intervals, reducing tick count to ~5–9 milestones.<br>2. *Standardized Milestone Label Formatting (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• In `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, intermediate milestone labels SHALL NOT repeat `" km"` or `" mi"` on every tick: (a) Metric: when `visibleSpan < 1500`, format as `"${currentDist.toInt()}m"`; when decimal (`currentDist % 1000.0 != 0.0`), format as `"%.1f"`; else format as `"${(currentDist / 1000.0).toInt()}"` (e.g. `"2"`, `"4"`, `"6"`); (b) Imperial: when decimal, format as `"%.1f"`; else format as `"${miles.toInt()}"` (e.g. `"2"`, `"4"`, `"6"`).<br>3. *Start and End Boundary Labels Parity (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• `TelemetryMetricGraph` SHALL instantiate `val distanceFormatter = remember(unit) { DistanceFormatter() }`.<br>• An explicit `endLabel` with units SHALL be rendered at `startPaddingPx + chartWidthPx - endLabelWidth`: `distanceFormatter.format_with_units(startDist + visibleSpan)` (e.g. `"17,82 km"`) in Distance domain, or `ElevationProfileZoomMath.formatTimeTick((startDist + visibleSpan).toLong())` in Time domain.<br>• When zoomed ($Z > 1.01$), an explicit `startLabel` with units SHALL be rendered at `startPaddingPx`: `distanceFormatter.format_with_units(startDist)` or `formatTimeTick(startDist.toLong())`.<br>4. *Dynamic Minimum Pixel Clearance & Decimation Algorithm (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• Intermediate milestone labels SHALL NOT render within 40 dp of the start padding (`tickX <= startPaddingPx + 40.dp.toPx()`) or within `endLabelWidth + 16.dp.toPx()` of the right chart edge (`startPaddingPx + chartWidthPx - tickX <= endLabelWidth + 16.dp.toPx()`).<br>• The renderer SHALL track `lastDrawnRightX`. An intermediate label SHALL only render if its left edge maintains at least 12 dp clearance: `labelLeft >= lastDrawnRightX + 12.dp.toPx()`, updating `lastDrawnRightX = labelLeft + labelWidth`. Colliding milestone labels SHALL be decimated (skipped) while underlying vertical grid lines continue to be rendered.<br>5. *Center-Aligned Milestone Positioning (`TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`)*:<br>• Milestone labels SHALL be centered under the tick mark: `nativeCanvas.drawText(label, tickX - (labelWidth / 2f), size.height - 4.dp.toPx(), axisTextPaint)`.<br>6. *Preservation of Core Invariants*:<br>• Horizontal padding geometry (50 dp start, 25 dp end), synchronized scrubbing cursor positioning, touch scrubbing coordinate mapping (`canvasXToDistance`), and 9-language localization parity remain 100% strictly preserved.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-UI-220`), extending and refining `REQ-UI-206` under Epic `ATT-111` (*Compact Post-Workout Visual Analytics & Graphs*).<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `061a4b35` (`ATT-1740`) introduced `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt` with an unconstrained X-axis loop; `ATT-1814` synchronized horizontal zoom.<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Secondary continuous graphs lacked collision avoidance, drew redundant `" km"` units on every tick, and omitted boundary labels, causing solid text collisions on workouts $\ge 10\text{ km}$.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Shared horizontal paddings, synchronized scrubbing, and invertibility of `ElevationProfileZoomMath` remain 100% strictly preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a workout with total distance 17.82 km,<br>• *When* `calculateAdaptiveDistanceStep` is evaluated in Metric mode,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `2_000f` (2 km tick step).<br>• *Given* `TelemetryMetricGraph` rendering continuous telemetry curves for a 17.82 km workout,<br>• *When* inspecting intermediate milestone labels along the bottom axis,<br>• *Then* labels SHALL render as `"2"`, `"4"`, `"6"`, etc., without repeating `" km"`, and an explicit end label (`"17,82 km"`) SHALL be anchored at the right chart boundary.<br>• *Given* any combination of workout length, zoom level, or screen width,<br>• *When* X-axis milestone labels are rendered,<br>• *Then* zero labels SHALL collide, overlap, or obscure boundary labels.<br><br>**Invariants**: Shared 50.dp start / 25.dp end padding geometry, synchronized touch scrubbing, and full unit test regression suite pass MUST NOT be broken. | Enforce adaptive X-axis milestone decimation (2 km step for 10-20km), collision clearance, standardized milestone formatting, and boundary start/end labels across Aftermath telemetry graphs. | `TelemetryMetricGraph.kt`, `ElevationProfileZoomMath.kt` | `TST-UI-174` | Verified |

| **REQ-CON-017** | **Barometric Altimeter Idempotent Calibration, Delta Shift Dispatch, Physical Sanity Limiting & Historical Workout Data Sanitization.** | The system SHALL eliminate barometric calibration oscillations, prevent runaway retroactive sample accumulation, enforce physical climb rate sanity limits, and sanitize contaminated historical workouts (ATT-1810):<br>1. *Absolute Baseline Correction Formulation (`AltitudeFromPressureDevice.java`)*:<br>• In `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.setAltitudeCorrection(double correctAltitude)`, `mAltitudeCorrection` SHALL be computed strictly relative to raw barometric pressure: $\text{newCorrection} = \text{correctAltitude} - \text{mLastRawAltitude}$.<br>• The method SHALL compute $\text{deltaOffset} = \text{newCorrection} - \text{mAltitudeCorrection}$, update $\text{mAltitudeCorrection} = \text{newCorrection}$, set $\text{mIsCalibrated} = \text{true}$, and publish $\text{mAltitudeSensor.newValue}(\text{mLastRawAltitude} + \text{mAltitudeCorrection})$.<br>• `ALTITUDE_CORRECTION_INTENT` SHALL be broadcast containing `ALTITUDE_CORRECTION_VALUE = deltaOffset` IF AND ONLY IF $|\text{deltaOffset}| \ge 0.1\text{ m}$. If $|\text{deltaOffset}| < 0.1\text{ m}$, the broadcast MUST be suppressed.<br>2. *Idempotent Altimeter Calibration Guard (`calibrate`)*:<br>• In `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.calibrate(double referenceAltitude)`, if `isCalibrated()` is true and current calibrated altitude is within $0.5\text{ m}$ of `referenceAltitude` ($|(\text{mLastRawAltitude} + \text{mAltitudeCorrection}) - \text{referenceAltitude}| < 0.5$), the method SHALL return `true` immediately without recomputing correction or broadcasting intents.<br>3. *Geofence Transition Calibration Gating (`TrackingTabsViewModel.kt`)*:<br>• In `TrackingTabsViewModel.kt`, altimeter calibration dispatch SHALL be gated on geofence transitions. The ViewModel SHALL maintain `lastCalibratedLocationId: Long?` and trigger `banalServiceRepository.calibrateAltimeter(closestItem.altitude)` IF AND ONLY IF `closestItem.id != lastCalibratedLocationId` or `!isCalibrated`.<br>• When exiting all geofences (`closestItem == null`), `lastCalibratedLocationId` SHALL be reset to `null`.<br>4. *Physical Climb/Descent Sanity Limiting & Atomic DB Transactions (`TrackerService.java`, `LiveWorkoutSession.java`)*:<br>• Retroactive sample shifting in `TrackerService.onReceive` SHALL be encapsulated within an explicit atomic SQLite transaction (`beginTransaction()` / `setTransactionSuccessful()` / `endTransaction()`).<br>• In `LiveWorkoutSession.applyAltitudeCorrection` and `TrackerService`, single retroactive shift offsets exceeding $|offset| > 500.0\text{ m}$ SHALL be rejected or clamped with an advisory warning.<br>• In `LiveWorkoutSession.recordStreamPoint` and `TrackerService`, altitude values outside human physical limits ($-500\text{ m} \dots +9000\text{ m}$) or vertical rate changes exceeding $|dh/dt| > 30\text{ m/s}$ ($108\text{ km/h}$) SHALL be clamped to the previous valid altitude sample.<br>5. *Historical Workout Data Sanitization & Export Resilience (`WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager.java`, `GPXFileWriter.java`, `TCXFileWriter.java`, `ElevationProfile.kt`)*:<br>• `WorkoutSummariesDatabaseManager` SHALL provide `sanitizeCorruptedAltitudeWorkouts()`: scanning existing workouts with feedback contamination (`maxAltitude > 4000.0m` and `minAltitude < 1000.0m`), adjusting corrupted leading trackpoints in `ALTITUDE_STREAM`, updating `TABLE_EXTREMA_VALUES` (MIN, MAX, AVG), and sanitizing corresponding `samplesTable` rows within an atomic SQLite transaction.<br>• `GPXFileWriter.java` and `TCXFileWriter.java` SHALL clamp non-physical altitude samples ($> 9000\text{ m}$ or vertical step spikes $> 100\text{ m}$) to the previous valid sample.<br>• In `ElevationProfile.kt` (`calculateElevationBounds`), non-physical start outliers SHALL be filtered from bounds computation, ensuring graph rendering auto-scales cleanly to real terrain (~480–530 m).<br>6. *Preservation of Core Invariants*:<br>• Null safety on cold start (`REQ-CON-013`), DEM elevation caching (`REQ-DAT-014`), start location counting (`REQ-DAT-015`), cockpit calibration badge feedback (`REQ-UI-199`), and 9-language localization parity MUST NOT be broken.<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement (`REQ-CON-017`), extending and refining `REQ-CON-013` and `REQ-UI-199` under Epic `ATT-111` / Altimeter Tracking.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Commit `53502c7a` (`ATT-1353`) and Sprint `2026-40.5` (`ATT-1617`).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: `setAltitudeCorrection` evaluated `currentAltitude` from `mAltitudeSensor.getValue()` which was already corrected, causing feedback oscillation and retroactive runaway shifts.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Cold-start null-safety, DEM caching, and cockpit badge feedback are 100% preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an `AltitudeFromPressureDevice` with `mLastRawAltitude = 450.0m` and default `mAltitudeCorrection = 0.0m`,<br>• *When* `setAltitudeCorrection(507.0)` is invoked,<br>• *Then* `mAltitudeCorrection` SHALL be set to $+57.0\text{ m}$, `ALTITUDE_CORRECTION_INTENT` SHALL be broadcast with extra value $57.0$, and the sensor value SHALL equal $507.0\text{ m}$.<br>• *Given* an `AltitudeFromPressureDevice` calibrated to 507.0m (`mAltitudeCorrection = 57.0m`),<br>• *When* `setAltitudeCorrection(507.0)` is invoked repeatedly interleaved with incoming pressure sensor measurements,<br>• *Then* `mAltitudeCorrection` SHALL remain $+57.0\text{ m}$ (zero oscillation to 0.0), sensor reading SHALL remain locked at $507.0\text{ m}$, and zero additional broadcasts SHALL be emitted.<br>• *Given* `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.calibrate(507.0)` executed successfully,<br>• *When* `calibrate(507.0)` is invoked again while within the same geofence,<br>• *Then* it SHALL return `true` immediately with zero broadcasts and zero DB shifts.<br>• *Given* an athlete inside a known location geofence emitting GPS updates every second,<br>• *When* `TrackingTabsViewModel.locationCalibrationStatus` evaluates sequential location emissions,<br>• *Then* `calibrateAltimeter` SHALL be invoked on initial geofence entry and SHALL NOT be dispatched repeatedly on continuous updates within the same location.<br>• *Given* incoming live tracking samples with an implausible vertical spike ($dh/dt > 30\text{ m/s}$) or single retroactive shift $> 500\text{ m}$,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL clamp the spike and reject runaway offsets.<br>• *Given* a stored workout with max altitude 7300m and min altitude 507m (*"Kurz zum Bäcker #14"*),<br>• *When* `sanitizeCorruptedAltitudeWorkouts()` is executed,<br>• *Then* `ALTITUDE_STREAM` and `TABLE_EXTREMA_VALUES` SHALL be re-aligned to real terrain (~480–530 m), and Aftermath rendering SHALL auto-scale cleanly.<br><br>**Invariants**: Cold-start null-safety, DEM caching, and cockpit badge feedback MUST NOT be broken. | Eliminate barometric calibration feedback oscillations, prevent runaway retroactive sample accumulation, enforce physical climb limits, and sanitize historical workout elevation profiles. | `AltitudeFromPressureDevice.java`, `TrackingTabsViewModel.kt`,
