When $< 5$ routes exist, filter chips SHALL be hidden.<br>• *1-Tap Activation & Deselection*: Tapping a route immediately sets it as `activeNavigatedRouteId` via `RoutesRepository.setActiveNavigatedRoute`. When a route is currently active, a dedicated "Route beenden / abwählen" action at the top clears the active route.<br>4. *Automated Route Detection Engine (`RouteAutoDetector`)*:<br>• During active recording when `activeNavigatedRouteId == null` and `routeAutoDetectEnabled == true`, the system SHALL evaluate the recorded GPS trajectory against saved routes.<br>• If cross-track distance is $\le 30\text{ m}$ for a continuous trajectory $\ge \text{threshold}$ (default $200\text{ m}$) and heading aligns ($\Delta \theta \le 35^\circ$), the system SHALL trigger a route detection event.<br>• In *Prompt* mode (default), the Cockpit displays an actionable banner/dialog allowing the athlete to activate or dismiss the route. In *Seamless* mode, the route is auto-joined immediately.<br>5. *Navigation Tuning Configuration*:<br>• `TuningPreferencesDataStore` and `AdvancedTuningDialog` SHALL provide user controls for `routeAutoDetectEnabled` (boolean, default true), `routeAutoJoinMode` (`PROMPT` vs `SEAMLESS`), and `routeAutoDetectThresholdMeters` (integer, default 200m).<br>6. *Localization Parity*:<br>• All user-facing strings SHALL maintain 100% parity across all 9 supported application locales (EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement only (`REQ-MAP-024`). No existing requirements modified.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-1835`, sprint `2026-40.14`, target release `V4.9.39`, Epic `ATT-66` (*[Epic] Improve Routes*).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: Route selection was disconnected from the tracking Cockpit, requiring multi-step navigation through the drawer and routes list; multiple routes starting from home lacked directional tie-breaking; and in-ride route following lacked automated detection.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: Existing `RoutesRepository` methods, map layers, tracking lifecycle, and 100% full-suite test pass rate remain preserved.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an athlete at home with 8 routes starting within 250m and beginning to ride east,<br>• *When* opening the Route Selector from the Cockpit,<br>• *Then* routes departing eastward with matching sport profile and recent usage appear at the top.<br>• *Given* a user with fewer than 5 saved routes,<br>• *When* opening the Route Selector,<br>• *Then* filter chips are hidden; when $\ge 5$ routes exist, filter chips are displayed.<br>• *Given* an active workout recording without an active route,<br>• *When* the athlete follows a saved route for 200m ($\Delta \text{dist} \le 30\text{m}$, $\Delta \text{bearing} \le 35^\circ$),<br>• *Then* the Cockpit prompts the athlete with an auto-detect banner to activate the route.<br>• *Given* an active route in navigation,<br>• *When* the athlete taps "Route beenden" in the sheet,<br>• *Then* `activeNavigatedRouteId` is cleared and active highlighting is removed.<br><br>**Invariants**: Route database schema, GPS recording integrity, and 100% full-suite test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Provide fast, frictionless route selection from the Cockpit with smart tie-breaking for home routes and automated in-ride route detection. | `RouteProximityRanker.kt`, `RouteAutoDetector.kt`, `RouteSelectorSheet.kt`, `SensorStatus.kt`, `SensorGridScreen.kt`, `TuningPreferencesDataStore.kt`, `AdvancedTuningDialog.kt` | `TST-MAP-026` | Verified |
| **REQ-MAP-025** | **Automatic DEM Elevation Enrichment for Imported GPX Routes Lacking Altitude Data.** | The system SHALL detect imported GPX route files lacking altitude data and automatically enrich their track points with authoritative elevation from the Open-Meteo Digital Elevation Model (DEM) API while guaranteeing robust batching, offline fallback resilience, and preservation of embedded GPX altitude (ATT-1502):<br>1. *Deficiency Detection & Elevation Preservation*:<br>• During GPX route parsing in `GpxRouteImporter`, the system SHALL evaluate track and route points (`trackPoints`).<br>• If at least one point contains non-null, non-zero elevation (`trackPoints.any { it.elevation != null && it.elevation != 0.0 }`), the system SHALL retain the embedded elevations verbatim and MUST NOT execute outbound network enrichment queries.<br>• If all points lack elevation or have flat 0.0m altitude (`trackPoints.none { it.elevation != null && it.elevation != 0.0 }`), the system SHALL trigger automatic DEM enrichment.<br>2. *Batching & Query Length Protection*:<br>• The system SHALL batch coordinates into chunks of at most 100 points (`MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 100`), preventing HTTP 414 (URI Too Long) errors on long routes ($N > 100$).<br>• Elevation queries SHALL be dispatched sequentially or with bounded concurrency via `ElevationService.getBatchElevationsAsync(chunk)` on `Dispatchers.IO`.<br>3. *Metrics Recalculation & Integrity*:<br>• Upon successful enrichment, the system SHALL update each `PathPoint.altitude` with retrieved DEM elevations, retaining point sequence and coordinates.<br>• The system SHALL recalculate the route's total `elevationGain` from the enriched profile and persist the updated gain in `RouteSummary`.<br>4. *Resilient Offline Fallback & Circuit Breaker Respect*:<br>• If network connectivity is unavailable, requests time out, HTTP 429 rate limit is encountered, or the circuit breaker is open, the system SHALL catch the failure gracefully and retain the track with default 0.0m altitude.<br>• The route import process SHALL NOT fail or throw exceptions due to elevation lookup failures.<br>5. *UI State & Localization Parity*:<br>• The import workflow SHALL notify the user of progress during enrichment.<br>• All new user-facing status messages SHALL maintain 100% translation parity across all 9 supported locales (EN, DE, ES, FR, IT, JA, NL, PL, PT).<br><br>**Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit**:<br>1. *Original Requirement ID & Target*: Net-new requirement only (`REQ-MAP-025`). No existing requirements modified.<br>2. *Historical Origin & Commit Trace*: Ticket `ATT-1502`, sprint `2026-40.14`, target release `V4.9.39`, Epic `ATT-66` (*[Epic] Improve Routes*).<br>3. *Root Reason for Existing Formulation*: GPX routes created by third-party planners often omit `<ele>` altitude tags, resulting in flat lines in `ElevationProfile`, zero elevation gain, and broken climb analytics.<br>4. *Preservation of Core Invariants*: GPX files with existing valid altitude tags remain untouched; Open-Meteo DEM rate limit backoff and circuit breaker in `ElevationService` are strictly respected; import never crashes or aborts on network error.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* an imported GPX route containing valid non-zero `<ele>` elevation tags,<br>• *When* parsed by `GpxRouteImporter`,<br>• *Then* `ElevationService` SHALL NOT be called, and original elevations SHALL be preserved.<br>• *Given* an imported GPX route where all points have null or 0.0m elevation,<br>• *When* parsed with active network connection,<br>• *Then* coordinates SHALL be chunked into batches ($\le 100$) and enriched via `ElevationService`, updating `PathPoint.altitude` and recalculating `RouteSummary.elevationGain` > 0m.<br>• *Given* an altitude-deficient GPX route imported while offline or when the DEM API returns an error / 429 rate limit,<br>• *When* enrichment fails,<br>• *Then* `GpxRouteImporter` SHALL NOT throw an exception, and the route SHALL successfully import as a 2D track with 0.0m altitude.<br><br>**Invariants**: Existing route database schema, GPX trackpoint ordering, `ElevationService` rate limiting and circuit breaker, and 100% full-suite test pass rate MUST NOT be broken. | Automatically enrich altitude-deficient GPX routes with DEM elevation data to restore elevation profiles, climb analytics, and gain calculations while providing resilient offline fallback. | `GpxRouteImporter.kt`, `ElevationService.kt`, `GpxImportViewModel.kt` | `TST-MAP-027` | Defined |

| **REQ-PRO-014** | **Unified 5-Stage ASPICE Dual-Agent Quality Gates & Automated Jira Workflow.** | The development workflow SHALL enforce explicit quality review gates embedded in the 5-state sub-task lifecycle (`Zu erledigen` -> `In Bearbeitung` -> `In Überprüfung` -> `Freigabe (Human)` -> `Erledigt`) across five sequential ASPICE stages for all ticket types (Bug, Improvement, Feature):<br>1. *Stage 1: Analysis (`[Analysis]`)*: Problem domain, user motivation, and side effects for features/improvements; root cause analysis (RCA) for bugs.<br>2. *Stage 2: Test Spec (`[Test-Spec]`)*: Requirement synchronization in `docs/requirements.md` and test specification in `docs/tests.md`.<br>3. *Stage 3: Implementation Plan (`[Impl-Plan]`)*: Architectural design, invariant protection, and test coverage mapping in `docs/engineering/plans/`.<br>4. *Stage 4: Implementation (`[Implementation]`)*: Software construction, self-documenting headers (KDoc/JavaDoc), and 9-language localization parity.<br>5. *Stage 5: Test (`[Test]`)*: Verification evidence, full clean-room regression testing (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`), and requirements/tests synchronization.<br>The workflow SHALL mandate that:<br>• *Automated Sub-Task Generation*: Sub-tasks are automatically created by Jira Automation upon the parent ticket entering each stage (agents SHALL NOT create lifecycle sub-tasks manually unless recovering from an untriggered state).<br>• *Description vs. Comment Discipline*: Agent 1 SHALL set the complete stage deliverable as the sub-task's **Description** and transition it to `In Überprüfung`. Agent 2 SHALL *always* conduct an independent gate audit upon sub-task entering `In Überprüfung`, post the audit report as a Jira comment (prefixed with `[Automated comment by AI Agent]`), and transition the sub-task to `Freigabe (Human)`.<br>• *Automated Parent Transitions*: Progression between stages SHALL occur autonomously once Agent 2's automated gate audit passes, transitioning the sub-task directly to `Erledigt` (via "freigabe"), whereupon Jira Automation automatically advances the parent ticket to the next stage and spawns the next sub-task. Sub-tasks do NOT require human approval.<br>• *Mandatory Lösungsversion (Fix Version/s)*: The workflow SHALL mandate that the `Lösungsversion` (*Fix Version/s*) is mandatory for all parent tickets across all issue types. The CLI tooling (`tools/jira_util.py`) SHALL display `Lösungsversion` on `show` and `list` and warn if missing. Agent 1 SHALL verify/set the `Lösungsversion` during Stage 5, and Agent 2 SHALL audit its presence during Gate 5 prior to human release approval and ticket closure.<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an assigned Jira ticket (Bug, Improvement, or Feature),<br>• *When* the ticket enters any lifecycle stage,<br>• *Then* Jira Automation SHALL automatically create the corresponding sub-task.<br>• *Given* Agent 1 finishes the stage deliverable and sets it as the sub-task Description,<br>• *When* the sub-task enters `In Überprüfung`,<br>• *Then* Agent 2 SHALL automatically audit the deliverable, post the review comment, and transition to `Freigabe (Human)`.<br>• *Given* Agent 2 audit PASS moving the sub-task to `Erledigt`,<br>• *When* transitioned,<br>• *Then* Jira Automation SHALL advance the parent ticket to the next stage and generate the next sub-task.<br>• *Given* a parent ticket entering Stage 5/6 release verification,<br>• *When* evaluated,<br>• *Then* the parent ticket's `Lösungsversion` SHALL be populated with the active release version, verified by Agent 2 in Gate 5.<br>**Invariants**: Moving parent tickets to `Erledigt` remains an inviolable human-only gate; sub-tasks transition directly to `Erledigt` upon automated Gate audit PASS; direct merges to `develop` without 100% sub-task completion remain strictly forbidden. | Ensure bidirectional ASPICE traceability, automated Jira lifecycle management, and independent AI quality audits without manual developer overhead. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules`, `tools/jira_util.py` | `TST-PRO-006`, `TST-PRO-008` | Verified |
| **REQ-PRO-015** | **Agent-Driven Git Branching, Conventional Commits, and Develop Merging Protocol.** | The development workflow SHALL mandate agent-driven git lifecycle management for all assigned Jira tickets:<br>1. *Branch Creation*: Upon starting work on any ticket, the agent SHALL verify or switch to `develop` and automatically create/checkout a dedicated branch adhering to naming standards (`feature/ATT-XXX` or `bugfix/ATT-XXX`).<br>2. *Conventional Commits*: The agent SHALL stage files (`git add`) and execute git commits (`git commit`) using the Conventional Commits format (`feat(...)`, `fix(...)`, `docs(...)`, etc.) with ticket reference and asterisk `*` bullet points.<br>3. *Develop Integration*: Upon completion and verification of all sub-tasks and human release approval, the agent SHALL switch to `develop` and merge the ticket branch into `develop` using a non-fast-forward merge (`git merge --no-ff <branch_name> -m "Merge branch '<branch_name>' into develop"`).<br>**Acceptance Criteria**:<br>• *Given* an assigned Jira ticket (`ATT-XXX`),<br>• *When* the agent begins development,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL create and switch to branch `feature/ATT-XXX` or `bugfix/ATT-XXX` off `develop`.<br>• *Given* approved changes across implementation and documentation,<br>• *When* committing work,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL execute `git commit` with a Conventional Commit message using `*` bullet points and ticket reference.<br>• *Given* 100% of sub-tasks in `Erledigt` and human sign-off,<br>• *When* concluding the ticket,<br>• *Then* the agent SHALL checkout `develop` and execute `git merge --no-ff <branch_name> -m "Merge branch '<branch_name>' into develop"`.<br>**Invariants**: Direct commits to `master` remain strictly forbidden; unreviewed code MUST NOT be merged into `develop`; sub-tasks complete autonomously via automated audit PASS while parent ticket release approval remains strictly reserved for the human user. | Ensure full git traceability, branch isolation, and non-fast-forward merge history without manual developer overhead. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules` | `TST-PRO-007` | Verified |
| **REQ-PRO-016** | **Inviolable ASPICE Human Decision Gates & Prevention of Premature Implementation Triggers.** | The development workflow SHALL strictly enforce human decision gate authority across all ASPICE stages, eliminating premature code execution caused by IDE test harness auto-approvals or synthetic prompts:<br>1. *Artifact Metadata Policy (`RequestFeedback: false`)*: Whenever an AI agent creates or updates plan, walkthrough, or analysis artifacts in the IDE, the agent SHALL ALWAYS specify `ArtifactMetadata: { RequestFeedback: false, UserFacing: true, ... }`. AI agents are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from specifying `RequestFeedback: true`. | **REQ-PRO-017** | **Process Hardening: Sub-Task Self-Sufficiency, Transition Sequencing, Discovery-First, and Git Finalization.** | The development workflow SHALL enforce four operational process safeguards across all ASPICE lifecycle stages:<br>1. *Sub-Task Self-Sufficiency*: Every lifecycle sub-task MUST stand on its own as an independent audit record. Transitioning a sub-task before its Description is populated is strictly forbidden.<br>3. *Automated Sub-Task Discovery (No Duplicate Creation)*: Agents SHALL inspect the parent ticket (`tools/jira_util.py show <Parent>`) to discover sub-tasks spawned by Jira Automation. | **REQ-PRO-018** | **Autonomous Multi-Model Independent Review Agent & Automated Gate Audits.** | The development workflow SHALL provide an autonomous, out-of-process review runner (`tools/review_agent.py`) capable of performing independent ASPICE quality gate audits (Gates 1 through 5) using external LLM providers (Google Gemini REST API via `.env.gemini` and Anthropic Claude Messages API via `.env.claude`):<br>1. *Architectural Independence & Memory Decoupling*: The review agent SHALL run in an independent Python process with zero shared conversational memory or prompt history with Agent 1, eliminating self-review confirmation bias.<br>2. *Gate Detection & Context Ingestion*: Given a sub-task key (`ATT-XXX`), the tool SHALL automatically determine the corresponding ASPICE stage and gate from the sub-task summary (`[Analysis]` -> Gate 1, `[Test-Spec]` -> Gate 2, `[Impl-Plan]` -> Gate 3, `[Implementation]` -> Gate 4, `[Test]` -> Gate 5). | **REQ-PRO-019** | **Multi-Account Jira Authentication, Atomic Resolution & Terminal Error Handling.** | The development workflow and CLI tooling (`tools/jira_util.py`, `tools/review_agent.py`) SHALL support role-specific Jira user credentials across three distinct agent roles: Agent 1 (Implementer), Agent 2 (Auditor), and Coordinator (Orchestrator):<br>1. *Role Credentials Configuration*: `.env.jira` SHALL support optional role-specific environment variables (`JIRA_AGENT1_USER`, `JIRA_AGENT1_TOKEN`, `JIRA_AGENT2_USER`, `JIRA_AGENT2_TOKEN`, `JIRA_COORDINATOR_USER`, `JIRA_COORDINATOR_TOKEN`) alongside base default credentials (`JIRA_USER`, `JIRA_TOKEN`).<br>2. *Atomic Resolution & Pair Fallback*: When resolving credentials for any role, if either the username or the API token for that role is missing, the system MUST NOT mix partial credentials; it SHALL print a clean diagnostic error to `sys.stderr` and exit with non-zero exit code (1).<br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* `.env.jira` configured with valid `JIRA_AGENT1_USER` and `JIRA_AGENT1_TOKEN`,<br>• *When* `jira_util.py` is invoked with role `agent1`,<br>• *Then* Jira HTTP requests SHALL use Basic Auth with Agent 1's username and token.<br>• *Given* `.env.jira` where `JIRA_AGENT2_USER` is configured but `JIRA_AGENT2_TOKEN` is unset or empty,<br>• *When* `jira_util.py` resolves credentials for `agent2`,<br>• *Then* the system SHALL atomically fall back to `JIRA_USER` and `JIRA_TOKEN`, logging an advisory notice to stderr.<br>• *Given* `.env.jira` where neither role credentials nor default `JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_TOKEN` are defined,<br>• *When* any Jira command is invoked,<br>• *Then* the tool SHALL halt immediately with error code 1 and exit.<br>**Invariants**: Moving any issue to `Erledigt` remains strictly prohibited across all roles; | **REQ-PRO-020** | **Role Locking, Precedence, Anti-Spoofing & Actor Comment Attribution.** | The development workflow and tooling SHALL enforce strict role boundaries, anti-spoofing constraints, and distinct comment attribution across agent roles:<br>1. *Precedence Rule*: The active role SHALL be determined strictly by: `CLI Flag (--as <role>)` > `Environment Variable (JIRA_ACTOR)` > `Script Default` (`agent1` for `jira_util.py`, `agent2` for `review_agent.py`).<br>2. *Role Locking & Anti-Spoofing*: `tools/review_agent.py` MUST be permanently hardwired to role `agent2`. | **REQ-PRO-022** | **Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Modification Hurdle.** | The development workflow and governance tooling SHALL enforce an explicit, auditable archaeological investigation before any existing requirement in `docs/requirements.md` is modified, relaxed, or replaced:<br>1. *Mandatory Archaeological Investigation*: Prior to proposing or applying changes to an existing requirement, the agent/engineer SHALL inspect the requirement's historical git commits (`git log -S <REQ-ID> docs/requirements.md` with timeout and depth bounds), associated Jira tickets, and architectural rationale to understand why the requirement was originally formulated in its current form (Chesterton's Fence principle).<br>2. *Machine-Checkable Archaeology Audit Section*: Any deliverable (Stage 1 Analysis, Stage 2 Test Specification, and Pull Request / Implementation description) that modifies an existing requirement MUST include a dedicated section titled `### Requirement Archaeology & Chesterton's Fence Audit` containing four mandatory structured fields:<br>• `Original Requirement ID & Target`: The exact requirement ID slated for alteration (e.g. `REQ-TRK-002`).<br>• `Historical Origin & Commit Trace`: Git commit hash(es), ticket key(s), and original defect/motivation.<br>• `Root Reason for Existing Formulation`: Explicit answer to *Why was this fence built?* (e.g. what bug, crash, regression, or schema constraint originally necessitated this exact phrasing).<br>• `Preservation of Core Invariants`: Explicit justification of *Why is it safe to modify now?*, proving that original system invariants remain protected or explaining why the historical constraint is obsolete.<br>3. *Independent Auditor Gate Enforcement (Gate 2)*: In `tools/review_agent.py`, the Gate 2 audit checklist SHALL explicitly inspect git diffs of `docs/requirements.md`. If existing requirement lines are modified (identified via diff hunk parsing), Gate 2 SHALL verify the presence, completeness, and validity of the archaeology section. Gate 2 SHALL issue `CHALLENGED` or `RECOMMEND REVISION` on any deliverable altering existing requirements without this complete archaeological justification.<br>4. *Dedicated Governance Verification Script (`tools/verify_requirement_governance.py`)*: A standalone verification utility implemented purely in Python 3 standard library SHALL analyze git diffs or deliverable text:<br>• Differentiates modified vs new requirements: detects whether existing requirement IDs were modified via diff analysis against `develop`.<br>• Validates section syntax: uses multiline regex parsing to verify that all four mandatory field labels exist with non-empty content.<br>• Deterministic exit codes: returns exit code `0` on compliance, exit code `1` with schema diagnostics on failure.<br>5. *Legacy Grandfathering*: Existing unmodified requirements remain valid as-is without requiring retroactive archaeology logs.<br><br>**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then)**:<br>• *Given* a branch with git diff modifications to an existing requirement line in `docs/requirements.md`,<br>• *When* `python3 tools/verify_requirement_governance.py` or `review_agent.py` Gate 2 evaluates the deliverable containing all 4 non-empty archaeology fields,<br>• *Then* the validation SHALL succeed with exit code 0.<br>• *Given* a branch modifying an existing requirement in `docs/requirements.md` where any of the 4 mandatory fields is missing or blank,<br>• *When* evaluated by `tools/verify_requirement_governance.py` or `review_agent.py` Gate 2,<br>• *Then* the verification script SHALL return exit code 1 with itemized schema errors, and Agent 2 SHALL issue a `CHALLENGED` or `RECOMMEND REVISION` audit verdict.<br>• *Given* a deliverable introducing only net-new requirements (new row with a new ID not existing in base),<br>• *When* evaluated by `tools/verify_requirement_governance.py`,<br>• *Then* the script SHALL classify the change as net-new and exit with code 0 without demanding an archaeology section.<br><br>**Invariants**: Zero external pip dependencies; APK runtime code and assets MUST NOT be modified; human decision gate authority remains inviolable. | Prevent regressions and accidental destruction of hard-won architectural protections by enforcing the Chesterton's Fence principle prior to modifying established requirements. | `docs/project_protocol.md`, `.cursorrules`, `tools/review_agent.py`, `tools/verify_requirement_governance.py` | `TST-PRO-015` | Verified |
